title: Pulmonary Embolism: The Critical Systemic Perspective
summary: Pulmonary Embolism (PE) is a life-threatening occlusion of the pulmonary vasculature, representing a major perioperative risk and a systemic emergency. This guide provides comprehensive clinical mastery, from Virchow's Triad to Purtscher-like retinopathy.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Pulmonary Embolism (PE) is the sudden occlusion of a pulmonary arterial vessel by an embolus (most commonly a thrombus from deep vein thrombosis, but also air, fat, or amniotic fluid). It is the third most common cause of cardiovascular death and a critical consideration in prolonged ophthalmic surgeries (e.g., orbital exenteration, complex retinal detachment repair).

branches: Stasis (Immobility, Obstructive Sleep Apnea, Ocular Surgery >2hrs)
Hypercoagulability (Factor V Leiden, Cancer, Pregnancy, OCP)

sections.title: Pathophysiological Sequence
content: 1. Embolus lodges in pulmonary artery
2. Increase in Pulmonary Vascular Resistance (PVR)
3. Right Ventricular (RV) afterload increase
4. RV dilation and septal shift to the left
5. Decreased Left Ventricular filling & Cardiac Output
6. V/Q mismatch and profound hypoxemia

sections.title: The Ophthalmic Connection: Purtscher-like Retinopathy
content: Rare manifestation of systemic microembolization (Fat/Air/Thrombotic).
Clinical Signs: Multiple Cotton Wool Spots (CWS), Purtscher Flecken (areas of inner retinal whitening), and intraretinal hemorrhages.
Mechanism: Microvascular occlusion and complement-mediated (C5a) leukoembolization.
Differential: Diabetics or Hypertensives can mimic, but Purtscher's is typically acute and associated with recent trauma or systemic emboli.
Prognosis: Often resolves spontaneously; visual outcome depends on macular ischemia.

sections.title: Clinical Symptoms Profile
content: Sudden Onset Dyspnea (82%)
Pleuritic Chest Pain (49%)
Cough (20%)
Hemoptysis (7%)
Syncope (indicates massive PE)
Apprehension / Impending Doom

sections.title: Diagnostic Red Flags
content: Hypotension (SBP < 90 mmHg)
Oxygen Saturation < 90% on Room Air
Tachycardia > 100 bpm in Ophthalmic Post-op
Unilateral Calf Swelling (DVT sign)
New onset Right Bundle Branch Block (ECG)

rows: Alternative Dx Less Likely than PE

sections.title: Diagnostic Investigation Strategy
content: 1. Risk Stratify: Use Wells Criteria or PERC rule.
2. Biomarkers: High-sensitivity D-dimer (only if Wells <= 4).
3. Imaging: CT Pulmonary Angiogram (CTPA) - Gold Standard.
4. Alternative Imaging: V/Q Scan if Renal Failure or Contrast Allergy.
5. Bedside Echo: Look for 'McConnell's Sign' (RV free wall akinesia).

sections.title: Management Protocol
content: 1. Stabilization: High-flow O2, fluid resuscitation (cautious).
2. Immediate Anticoagulation: LMWH (Enoxaparin 1mg/kg) or UFH.
3. Thrombolysis: Alteplase (tPA) reserved for Massive PE.
4. Long-term Anticoagulation: DOACs (Rivaroxaban, Apixaban) for 3-6 months.
5. Interventional: Catheter-directed thrombectomy for high-risk cases.

rows: ECG shows ST-elevation/depression; Troponin rise pattern.
Acute onset, absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation.
Tearing back pain, unequal BP in arms, widened mediastinum.
Normal SpO2, circumoral tingling, normal D-dimer.

content.explanation: T: Tachycardia, H: Hemoptysis, R: Reduced SaO2, O: Orthopnea, M: Mid-line chest pain (Pleuritic), B: Breathlessness, I: Increased RR (Tachypnea).

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Pearls
content: S1Q3T3 is famous but only present in <20% of cases.
A normal CXR in a hypoxic patient should strongly raise suspicion of PE.
D-dimer has high sensitivity but poor specificity; it is for 'ruling out' only.
The PESI score (Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index) helps decide on home vs hospital care.
In Ophthalmic surgery, avoid retrobulbar blocks in patients on full anticoagulation.

sections.title: Surgical/Procedural Interventions
content: Inferior Vena Cava (IVC) Filters: Used if anticoagulation is contraindicated (e.g., immediate post-op bleeding risk).
Surgical Embolectomy: Indicated for massive PE when thrombolysis fails or is contraindicated.
Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis (CDT): Lower doses of tPA delivered directly to the clot.

rows: Tenecteplase in submassive PE reduces decompensation but increases bleed risk.
Rivaroxaban is non-inferior to standard therapy (Enox/Warfarin).
Validated the use of D-dimer adjusted by clinical probability.
